title: The past tense
description: Say what you did: the four verb groups in preteritum, strong verbs, and time words like igår.

guide.summary: Preteritum tells what happened at a finished time: igår, förra veckan. The form is the same for every person; the ending depends on the verb group, which the present tense gives away. This page has the four regular endings, the strong verbs that change their vowel, four common irregulars, and word order with time words.

sections.title: Four groups and the strong verbs
sections.text: The Swedish past, preteritum, has one form for every person: jag, du, hon, vi and de all say pratade. What changes is the ending, and the present tense tells you which group a verb belongs to. Every verb note in the deck lists present, past and supine, so you can always check.
steps: Look at the present: -ar points to group 1.
Present in -er or -r with a stem ending in a consonant: group 2, -de or -te.
A short verb ending in a vowel: group 3, -dde.
Strong verbs change the vowel and have to be learnt.
watch: Never change the verb for the person: hon pratade, de pratade.
The supine (pratat, köpt) is not the past on its own; it needs har or hade.

sections.title: Group 1: -ade
sections.text: Verbs whose present ends in -ar keep the a of the infinitive and add -de. This is the biggest group and every new verb usually joins it.
steps: Check that the present ends in -ar.
Take the infinitive with its a.
Add -de.
watch: The a stays: städade, not städde.
One d only: lyssnade, not lyssnadde.

sections.title: Group 2a: -de after a voiced sound
sections.text: Verbs with -er in the present drop the -a of the infinitive to get the stem. If the stem ends in a voiced sound such as g, r, l, m, n or v, add -de.
steps: Check that the present ends in -er or just -r.
Drop the -a to find the stem.
The stem ends in a voiced sound: add -de.
watch: A double m or n before the -a becomes single: glömde, kände.
Not -ade: ringer is group 2, so never ringade.

sections.title: Group 2b: -te after k, p, s, t
sections.text: When the stem of a group 2 verb ends in a voiceless sound, k, p, s or t, the d hardens to t. Say köpde aloud and you feel why.
steps: Drop the -a to find the stem.
The last letter is k, p, s or t: add -te.
Otherwise use -de.

examples.en: We went to work by bus.

watch: Only group 2: titta ends in t, but tittar is group 1, so tittade.
Tänkte and tyckte are -te because of the k.

sections.title: Group 3: short verbs, -dde
sections.text: Short verbs of one syllable that end in a vowel add -dde: the double d keeps the vowel long. Not every short verb belongs here: gå, se and ta are strong.
steps: Is the verb one syllable ending in a vowel?
Check the deck note: does the past end in -dde?
If so, add -dde.

examples.sv: Jag trodde att du var hemma.
examples.en: I thought you were at home.

watch: Gå, se and ta look the same but are strong: gick, såg, tog.

sections.title: Strong verbs: a new vowel
sections.text: Strong verbs change their vowel in the past and add no ending. Many of the most common verbs are strong, so learn them as a set: the deck note gives the past.
steps: Is the verb in the table or marked with a new vowel in its note?
Use the past from the note.
Add nothing to it.
watch: No -de on a strong verb: skrev, not skrivde.
Do not confuse the past with the supine: drack, but har druckit.

sections.title: Vara, ha, göra, säga
sections.text: Four very common verbs have pasts of their own. Säga has two forms: sa is what most people say and write, sade is the full form.
steps: Recognise one of the four verbs.
Use its past from the table.
watch: Gjorde is spelled with gj and sounds like jorde.

sections.title: Time words: igår, förra veckan
sections.text: The past goes with words that point back in time: igår, igår kväll, förra veckan, i helgen. When one of them starts the sentence, the verb still comes second, so the subject moves after it.
steps: Choose the past verb form.
If a time word starts the sentence, put the verb right after it.
Put the subject after the verb.

examples.en: Yesterday we had dinner at home.

examples.sv: Förra veckan åkte jag till Stockholm.
examples.en: Last week I went to Stockholm.

watch: Igår jag åt is wrong: the verb comes second.
Igår can also be written i går.

steps: Check that the present ends in -ar.
Keep the a of the infinitive and add -de.
Drop the -a of the infinitive to get the stem.
Check the last sound: voiced means -de.
Drop the -a of the infinitive to get the stem.
If it ends in k, p, s or t, add -te.
Check the verb is one short syllable ending in a vowel.
Add -dde.
Recognise a strong verb from the table or the deck note.
Use its past with the new vowel and no ending.
Recognise vara, ha, göra or säga.
Use the form in the table: var, hade, gjorde, sa.
Use a past verb with igår or förra veckan.
If the time word comes first, put the verb second and the subject after it.

exercises.hint: Pratar ends in -ar in the present. What does that tell you about the past?
exercises.feedback: Verbs with -ar in the present add -ade.
exercises.explanation: Jag pratade: prata + -de, so the past ends in -ade.

mistakes.why: Pratar is the present: I talk, I am talking. The past needs a new ending.
Pratat is the supine, used after har or hade: jag har pratat. On its own it is not a past tense.
The -te ending belongs to verbs whose stem ends in k, p, s or t without an -ar present. Pratar keeps its a.

exercises.hint: Present: städar. Group 1 keeps the a.
exercises.feedback: Group 1 verbs add -de to the whole infinitive: -ade.

mistakes.why: Städar is the present. Igår puts the action in the past.
Städat is the supine, which needs har or hade in front of it.
The a of städa is part of the stem and stays: group 1 never drops it.

exercises.hint: Lyssnar is the present. Which form is the past?
exercises.feedback: Lyssna is group 1: the past ends in -ade.

mistakes.why: Lyssnar is the present: she listens. The sentence tells what she did one evening.
Lyssnat is the supine. It only works after har or hade.
Only short verbs like bo and tro double the d. Lyssna just adds one d after its a.

exercises.hint: Worked: jobba is group 1. At home is one word.
exercises.feedback: Jobba keeps its a and adds -de.

mistakes.why: Jobbar is the present. With igår the verb has to be in the past too.
When igår comes first, the verb must come second, before jag.
Jobbat is the supine and needs har in front of it.

exercises.instruction: Put the sentence in the past.
exercises.hint: Öppnar ends in -ar: change -ar to -ade.
exercises.feedback: Group 1: -ar in the present, -ade in the past.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged, still in the present.
Öppnat is the supine. Without har it is not a sentence.
The a of öppna stays before the past ending.

exercises.hint: Watch is titta på. Pick the past tile.
exercises.explanation: Vi tittade på en film: titta + -de.

mistakes.why: Tittar is the present: we are watching. The English is in the past.
Titta needs på before what you watch.

exercises.hint: The stem is stäng-. Is its last sound voiced or voiceless?
exercises.feedback: Stäng- ends in a voiced sound, so it takes -de.

mistakes.why: The -te ending is for stems ending in k, p, s or t. Stäng- ends in a voiced g.
Stängt is the supine, used after har: hon har stängt.
Stänger is the present.
Stänga has stänger in the present, not stängar, so it is not group 1.

exercises.hint: Present: ringer. Drop the -a, look at the last sound of ring-.
exercises.feedback: Ring- ends in a voiced sound: -de.

mistakes.why: G is voiced, so the ending is not -te.
The present is ringer, not ringar, so this is not group 1.
Ringt is the supine: vi har ringt.

exercises.hint: Present: hör. The stem ends in r.
exercises.feedback: R is voiced: add -de to the stem.

mistakes.why: R is a voiced sound, so the ending is not -te.
Hört is the supine: jag har hört.
Hör is the present.
Höra has hör in the present, not hörar, so it does not take -ade.

exercises.hint: Present: kör. What kind of sound is r?

mistakes.why: The -te ending follows k, p, s or t. R is voiced.
A double d is only for stems ending in a vowel, like bo and tro.
Köra has kör in the present, not körar, so it is not group 1.

exercises.hint: Look at the last sound of the stem glöm-.
exercises.feedback: M is voiced, so the ending is -de.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: m is voiced, so -te is wrong here.
Glömt is the supine and needs har.
A double m only comes before a vowel, as in glömmer. Before d it is single.

exercises.hint: Close is stänga. The door is dörren.
exercises.feedback: Stäng- ends in a voiced sound: -de.

mistakes.why: G is voiced, so the ending is not -te.
Stänger is the present: she closes.
The door is a specific door, so Swedish uses the definite form with -en.

exercises.hint: Present: köper. The stem köp- ends in p.
exercises.feedback: After k, p, s or t the ending is -te.

mistakes.why: P is voiceless, so -de is not used: it would be hard to say.
Köpa has köper in the present, not köpar, so it is not group 1.
Köpt is the supine: du har köpt.

exercises.hint: Present: åker. The stem åk- ends in k.

mistakes.why: After k the ending changes to -te.
Åka has åker in the present, not åkar, so it is not group 1.
Åkt is the supine: vi har åkt.
Åker is the present.

exercises.hint: Present: hjälper. What is the last letter of the stem?

mistakes.why: P is voiceless, so the ending is not -de.
Hjälpa has hjälper in the present, not hjälpar.
Hjälpt is the supine and needs har.

exercises.source: Jag tänkde på dig hela dagen.
answers: Jag tänkte på dig hela dagen.
exercises.hint: Tänk- ends in k. Which ending follows k?

answers: Jag tänkde på dig hela dagen.
mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: after k the d hardens.

answers: Jag tänkade på dig hela dagen.
mistakes.why: Tänka has tänker in the present, so it does not take -ade.

answers: Jag tänkt på dig hela dagen.
mistakes.why: Tänkt is the supine and needs har.

exercises.hint: Köp- ends in p.

mistakes.why: After p the ending is not -de.

exercises.instruction: Put the sentence in the past.
exercises.hint: Läser is group 2. The stem läs- ends in s.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged, still in the present.
After s the ending is not -de.
Läst is the supine and needs har.

exercises.hint: Bo is a short verb that ends in a vowel.
exercises.feedback: Short verbs ending in a long vowel add -dde.

mistakes.why: A short verb like bo needs a double d after its vowel.
Bo is not group 1: its present is bor, not boar.
Bott is the supine: de har bott.
Bor is the present.

exercises.hint: Tro is one syllable and ends in a vowel.

mistakes.why: The d is doubled after the short verb tro.
Tro has tror in the present, so it does not take -ade.
Trott is the supine: jag har trott.
Tror is the present. The rest of the sentence is in the past.

exercises.source: Vi ____ i Göteborg i tre år.
exercises.hint: Bo ends in a vowel. How many d?

mistakes.why: One d is not enough after bo.
Bo is not group 1: its present is bor.
Bor is the present: we live there now.

exercises.instruction: Put the sentence in the past.
exercises.source: De bor i ett litet hus.
answers: De bodde i ett litet hus.
exercises.hint: Bor comes from bo, a short verb.

answers: De bor i ett litet hus.
mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged.

answers: De bode i ett litet hus.
mistakes.why: After bo the d is doubled.

answers: De bott i ett litet hus.
mistakes.why: Bott is the supine and needs har.

exercises.hint: Live (in a place) is bo.

mistakes.why: After bo the d is doubled.
Bor is the present: she lives there now.
Leva means to be alive. Living in a place is bo.

exercises.hint: Tro is a short verb ending in a vowel.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: one d is not enough after tro.
Tror is the present. Correct the past, do not change the tense.

exercises.hint: Skriva is strong: the vowel changes and nothing is added.
exercises.feedback: Look up the past in the verb note: skriver, skrev, skrivit.
exercises.explanation: Jag skrev: i becomes e, no ending.

mistakes.why: Skriva is a strong verb: it changes its vowel instead of adding -de.
Skrivit is the supine: jag har skrivit.
Skriver is the present.

exercises.hint: Komma is strong and gets shorter in the past.
exercises.explanation: Hon kom: the -mer ending goes and the past is one short word.

mistakes.why: Komma is strong: no -de is added.
Kommit is the supine: hon har kommit.
Kommer is the present.

exercises.hint: Gå looks like bo, but it is strong.
exercises.explanation: Vi gick: a completely new form.

mistakes.why: Gå looks like a short group 3 verb, but it is strong and changes its form.
Gått is the supine: vi har gått.
Går is the present.

exercises.hint: Komma is strong: no ending is added.
exercises.explanation: Erik kom hem: strong past, no ending.

mistakes.why: Strong verbs never take -de.
Kommit is the supine and needs har.
Kommer is the present, but igår points to the past.

exercises.source: Jag ____ en bra film i helgen.
exercises.hint: Se is strong: the vowel changes to å.
exercises.explanation: Jag såg: se changes to såg.

mistakes.why: Se looks like bo, but it is strong: no -dde.
Sett is the supine: jag har sett.
Ser is the present.

exercises.hint: Take is ta, a strong verb.
exercises.explanation: De tog bussen: ta becomes tog.

mistakes.why: Ta is strong, not a short group 3 verb.
Tagit is the supine and needs har.
Tar is the present.

exercises.source: I wrote a letter to Mum.
answers: Jag skrev ett brev till mamma.
exercises.hint: Skriva is strong.

answers: Jag skrivde ett brev till mamma.
mistakes.why: Skriva is strong and does not take -de.

exercises.hint: Dricka is strong: i becomes a.
exercises.explanation: Barnen drack: the vowel changes, no ending.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: dricka is strong.
Druckit is the supine and needs har.

exercises.hint: Vara is the most irregular verb: är in the present.
exercises.explanation: Vi var: one short form for every person.

mistakes.why: Är is the present: we are.
Varit is the supine: vi har varit.
Varade comes from vara meaning to last, as in the film lasted. Be has its own short past.

exercises.hint: The past of göra changes its spelling at the start.
exercises.explanation: Du gjorde: written with gj, said like jorde.

mistakes.why: Göra changes to gj in the past: the ö becomes o.
Gjort is the supine: du har gjort.
Gör is the present.

exercises.source: Vi ____ (ha) en fin semester i Spanien.
exercises.hint: Ha keeps its a and adds -de.

mistakes.why: Ha takes a single d, unlike bo and tro.
Haft is the supine: vi har haft.
Har is the present.

exercises.hint: Säga has a short past in speech and writing.
exercises.explanation: Hon sa: the everyday past of säga. Sade is the longer written form.

mistakes.why: Säga is irregular: the vowel changes and the g disappears.
Sagt is the supine: hon har sagt.
Säger is the present, but the rest of the sentence is past.

exercises.instruction: Put the sentence in the past.
exercises.hint: Är is the present of vara.
exercises.explanation: Jag var trött: vara in the past.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged.
Varit is the supine and needs har.
Vara meaning be has a short irregular past.

exercises.hint: Say is säga, an irregular verb.
exercises.explanation: Han sa hej. Sade is the same word, written in full.

mistakes.why: Säga does not add -de to its stem.
Säger is the present.
Sagt is the supine and needs har.

exercises.hint: The past of göra is spelled with gj.
exercises.explanation: Vad gjorde du igår: the ö becomes o after gj.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged.
Gjort is the supine and needs har.

exercises.hint: Förra veckan means last week: past tense, and the verb stays second.
exercises.feedback: Time word first, then verb, then subject.

mistakes.why: Åker is the present. Förra veckan is in the past.
Vi is already after the blank: the gap is only for the verb.
After k the ending is -te.

exercises.instruction: Choose the time word that fits.
exercises.hint: Köpte is past. Which word points to the past?
exercises.feedback: The past tense goes with time words like igår and förra veckan.
exercises.explanation: Igår köpte jag en ny telefon: past verb, past time word.

mistakes.why: Imorgon means tomorrow. It cannot go with köpte, which is past.
Nu means now. It does not fit a verb in the past.

exercises.instruction: Start with Igår and put the verb in the past.
exercises.hint: Two changes: the past of ringa, and the verb second.
exercises.feedback: After a time word the verb comes before the subject.
exercises.explanation: Igår ringde jag mamma: ring- + -de, verb in second place.

mistakes.why: The verb must be the second element: after igår comes the verb, then jag.
Ringer is the present. Igår needs the past.
G is voiced, so the ending is not -te.

exercises.source: Last week we cleaned the house.
exercises.hint: Start with the time words, then the verb.
exercises.feedback: The verb comes second, right after förra veckan.
exercises.explanation: Förra veckan städade vi huset: städa + -de, verb second.

mistakes.why: After förra veckan the verb comes before vi.
Städar is the present. Last week needs the past.

exercises.hint: Drink is dricka, a strong verb. If igår comes first, the verb comes next.
exercises.explanation: Igår drack jag kaffe: strong past, verb in second place.

mistakes.why: After igår the verb must come before jag.
Dricka is strong: it changes its vowel instead of taking -te.
Dricker is the present.

exercises.source: Igår jag såg Lars i parken.
answers: Igår såg jag Lars i parken.
I går såg jag Lars i parken.
exercises.hint: Find the verb. Is it in second place?
exercises.feedback: After a time word, the verb comes before the subject.
exercises.explanation: Igår såg jag Lars: verb second.

answers: Igår jag såg Lars i parken.
mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: the verb is in third place.

answers: Igår ser jag Lars i parken.
mistakes.why: The verb is already in the past. Move it, do not change the tense.

exercises.hint: Igår kväll means last night. Äta is strong.
exercises.explanation: Igår kväll åt vi middag: äta in the past.

mistakes.why: Äter is the present: we eat. Igår kväll is in the past.
Ätit is the supine and needs har.
Äta is strong: no -te ending.
